summary:
17 research items cleared the filter out of 60 raw tweets over the 4-day window (43 dropped as empty-banks noise, mostly MikeZaccardi's high-frequency price/sector charts; no neilksethi/neilksethinew items this cycle; no duplicates found).

Goldman dominates with a rates/equity grab-bag: a 25bp September FOMC hike now expected, GDP growth holding near 2.2%, core PCE cooling toward 2.5%, a reaffirmed S&P 500 8000 year-end target and $385 2027 EPS, an equity duration/rate-sensitivity framework (ERP at 3%, ~75% of SPX value from cash flows 10+ years out), historical hiking-cycle equity drawdowns, an M&A rebound to $1.4T YTD, and steady central-bank gold buying.

Single items round out the window: Morgan Stanley on resilient real GDP growth despite two years of supply-side shocks; Apollo's Slok on a savings glut flipping into a savings shortage that keeps long rates high; and Hartnett/BofA flagging private-client cash allocation at a record low.

Counts: Goldman 14, Apollo/Slok 1, BofA 1, Morgan Stanley 1.

items.author: MikeZaccardi
items.text:
From a savings glut to a savings shortage 🔄

When capital was abundant, projects competed for it with lower returns. Now, with massive data center and infrastructure builds, capital is scarce and demands a higher yield 📈

Expect long-term rates to stay high 💸 Torsten at Apollo https://t.co/GhIpUeXvRG
